meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: Often used with 하다.

examples.trans: Please don't worry.
I have many worries.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (급히).

examples.text: 내 말이 그 말이다! 걔는 뭐 이렇게 급히 할 말이 있다고 이 비 오는데 말이야!
examples.trans: That is my exact point! What could she possibly need to say so urgently in this pouring rain?!

examples.text: 제가 지금은 집에 뭘 급히 가지러 올라가는 길이었거든요. 그것만 가지고 내려오면 그냥 차를 빼서 가면 돼서요.
examples.trans: Right now I am rushing upstairs just to grab something—as soon as I bring it down, I am pulling the car straight out anyway.
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?
I want to turned off right now.
How about trying to turned off together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to be late, to be behind schedule
meanings.note: Takes attributive -은 (늦은) before a noun.

examples.trans: I was a little late today.
Sorry for the late hour.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Used as casual question (뭐래니?).

examples.text: 얘 뭐래니? 그럼 그렇지, 아유 내 팔자야!
examples.trans: What are you talking about? Figures—honestly, just my luck!
Let us do that (what is he saying) right away.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 아무도 관심이 없는 판에 누가 오겠다고 경합을 붙니?
examples.trans: When nobody cares if our show disappears, who would compete to join?

meanings.note: Used with 오다 or 내리다.

examples.trans: It is raining.

meanings.note: Used as connective -어가지고 (사가지고!).

examples.text: 내가 무슨 한가하게 영화를 본다고 이렇게 팝콘까지 사가지고! 신디 기다린다며?

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.text: 아유 설마, 전화 좀 해 봐!
examples.trans: Oh come on, surely not—give him a call right now!
Here the word for 'oh goodness' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?

meanings.note: Exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh my, so nice to meet you!

meanings.note: Used as noun (얼마).

examples.text: 아, 마지막에 이거 넣으라고, 한편 신디는 얼마 전 특집쇼 녹화 중 담당 여자 피디인 티모 피디의 실수로 부상을 입어 입원을 한 바 있다.

examples.trans: Let's go watch a movie.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.

meanings.note: Used as causal -해서 (욱해서).
